claims.text: Surface functionalization of a nanostructured electrocatalyst with a noble-metal oxide will enhance HER catalytic activity.
Surface functionalization of a nanostructured electrocatalyst with a noble-metal oxide will enhance HOR catalytic activity.
The proposed surface functionalization will improve electrocatalyst durability.
The proposed intervention is deposition of a noble-metal oxide, such as iridium oxide, by a sol-gel method at a loading of 0.5 mg/cm².
The catalyst is intended to operate from 0 to 1.5 V versus RHE and from 0 to 100 mA/cm².
Noble-metal-oxide surface functionalization increases the catalyst surface area.
Increased surface area provides more active sites for HER and HOR.
Surface functionalization optimizes the catalyst surface energy.
Optimized surface energy improves hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
Improved hydrogen adsorption and desorption leads to enhanced HER and HOR catalytic activity.
The functionalized catalyst will show a 30% increase in exchange current density relative to a traditional electrocatalyst such as platinum.
The functionalized catalyst will show a 25% increase in electrochemical durability over 1000 cycles relative to a traditional electrocatalyst such as platinum.
The surface functionalization will be effective only if the nanostructured surface remains stable under the operating conditions.
